results.3: all four arms: exit 3, no file change. The wording differs by arm, e.g. "troupe: agents.coder.<<: '<<' is the merge key; troupe never writes merge keys; no file changed" and "troupe: error: agents.coder.<<: troupe never writes a merge key (<<)"

results.1:
exit 0; prints:
model: opus
'true': on
'null': x
'1e3': y
'<<': z
results.2:
exit 0; prints the same quoted keys even though the file has them unquoted:
model: opus
'true': on
'null': x
'1e3': y
'<<': z
results.3:
three arms: exit 0; prints:
model: opus
'true': on
'null': x
'1e3': y
one arm: exit 0; also quotes the values:
model: opus
'true': 'on'
'null': x
'1e3': 'y'

context.in_practice: On route 2, `config show` displays the keys quoted, but the file itself contains plain `true:`, `null:` and `1e3:`. Any other tool or person reading the file will see those as a boolean, a null and a number, not as names. Routes 1 and 3 write the quotes into the file. Route 3 also refuses to create a `<<` key at all, while routes 1 and 2 store it quoted.
context.stakes: When someone sets a config key named like `true`, `null`, `1e3` or `<<`, the question is whether the YAML file on disk still holds that key as plain text. Unquoted, other YAML readers will load such a key as a boolean, null, number or merge key instead of a name.
context.tradeoff: Route 1 quotes every ambiguous key and allows a quoted `<<`. Route 2 only guards `<<`, so the file is left with keys that other readers take as non-strings. Route 3 quotes ambiguous keys too but rejects `<<` with exit 3, and one arm also quotes some values in `show`.

plan_why: Adds new keys spelled true, null, 1e3 and << under a mapping whose existing key is plain. The file diffs show which keys each route quotes: all four, only <<, or none. The final show reveals whether unquoted keys come back as booleans, nulls or floats, or stop the config from loading.
routes: Quote any new key whose plain form would not read back as a string
